executive_summary: Your AMBER status is driven entirely by peer-level exposure to geopolitical shocks, not by macro weakness or supplier-specific failures. The core issue is concentration: five suppliers clustered in China face identical US-China trade and Taiwan risks (Porton, Huizhou BYD, Smoore, EVE Energy, and IP Sun), while three others depend on single-country vulnerabilities that lack redundancy (Stora Enso on NATO proximity, Sappi on South African infrastructure, ITC on India-Pakistan tensions). The two China-based EMS providers with critical battery exposure warrant immediate attention for dual-sourcing or nearshoring pilots, since a Taiwan supply shock or tech export freeze would cripple production. The nicotine and printing substrate risks are lower-urgency unless geopolitical temperatures spike; focus near-term energy on mapping alternative suppliers in Southeast Asia or Eastern Europe for the EMS and battery categories, then tier the rest by your contractual flexibility and safety stock buffers.
